context_requirements: Ras-pathway or Rheb/mTOR dependence for antiproliferative response
Wild-type or H/N-Ras rather than K-Ras-driven background for stronger sensitivity
Intact stress and cell-cycle checkpoint machinery
falsifiers: No change in cholesterol biosynthesis genes at 6 h
No proliferation or G2/M gene changes at 24 h
No stress-response gene induction at either time
Uniform strong response across all nine lines

evidence.supports: Farnesyl transferase inhibitor R115777 inhibits growth of many human tumor cell lines and blocks Ras/lamin processing
Farnesyl transferase inhibitor SCH66336 inhibits proliferation and enhances apoptosis in BCR-ABL-positive cells
FTI/GGTI combinations block Ki-Ras prenylation and induce apoptosis in pancreatic tumor cells
Lonafarnib inhibits Rheb farnesylation and mTOR signaling, linking FTI to mTOR-dependent growth
SCH66336 inhibits BCR/ABL transformation, Ras effector pathways, and causes G2/M blockade

changes: Moved PLK1, CCNB1, CCNA2, BIRC5, AURKA, TOP2A, UBE2C, CDC20, BUB1B, KIF20A from late_up to removed: these are proliferation/G2-M genes and should be down, not up, under a transferase inhibitor causing G2/M arrest.

Removed generic proliferation and stress genes from proximal lists: DNAJB1, HSPA1A, HSPB1, FOS, JUN, EGR1, ATF5, DDIT4, TRIB3, SQSTM1, NFKBIA, IER3, GADD45B, ZFP36, HMOX1 are generic stress/proliferation markers, not proximal to transferase inhibition.
Removed cholesterol biosynthesis genes HMGCR, HMGCS1, FDFT1, INSIG1, ACAT2, EBP, NSDHL from proximal_down: no evidence links transferase inhibition to immediate cholesterol biosynthesis repression.
Kept late_up CDKN1A, GADD45A, TSC22D3, SESN1 as plausible secondary stress/cell-cycle arrest genes.
Kept late_down proliferation genes CCND1, CCNE2, CDK2, CDK4, CDK6, MYC, E2F2, PCNA, MCM3, MTHFD2, PAICS, GMNN as consistent with growth inhibition.
Line responses left unchanged: no line-specific data in abstracts to contradict moderate/weak assignments.
